description: Two-quark Hopf-class vs three-quark Borromean SDP-cost-proxy comparison across the metallic ladder.  Hopf, trefoil 3_1, and 5_1 are all torus links with V_hyp = 0, so their cost contribution to any SDP weighted by V_hyp vanishes identically — they're 'free' to form.  The Borromean carries the full V_hyp = 8·G ≈ 7.33 floor.  This is the structural reason 2-quark Hopf-class states are systematically cheaper than the 3-quark Borromean: NOT a metallic-piecewise effect, but a topological-volume effect at the ground state.
verdict: Hopf-class states are cheaper than Borromean by the FULL hyperbolic-volume floor, not because of metallic-ladder structure.  The volume hierarchy V_hyp(Hopf)=0 < V_hyp(4_1)=2.03 < V_hyp(Borromean)=7.33 is the structural ordering, independent of q within the metallic range tested.  Metallic ratios do NOT cross this ordering — Borromean stays the heaviest at every q in (q_0, delta_bronze).
limitations: Markov-trace evaluations on n=2 σ_1^k are exact (1-dim reps).
Borromean (2,1) character uses a Chebyshev-like closed-form approximation that captures leading-order structure; sub-leading corrections do not affect the qualitative ordering.
'SDP cost' is the (|tr_M| × V_hyp) proxy; the true SDP optimal value needs the full per-nucleus character witness.
metallic_finding: Within the (q_0, delta_bronze) range, metallic ratios do NOT induce any crossing of the cost ordering Hopf < 4_1 < Borromean.  This is one more piece of evidence that real-q metallic structure is purely algebraic (Hecke-scalar integrality) and does not control the SDP cost landscape.
